name: EquipmentManager
src_typeComment: Typed equipment slots (Weapon/Head/Body/Accessory — see EquipSlotType) composed on top of an EXISTING Inventory rather than duplicating item storage: equipping REMOVES one from the inventory, unequipping ADDS it back — the inventory stays the single source of truth for "does the player own this."

src_serialized.name: inventory
src_serialized.tooltip: Items equipped here are removed from / returned to this inventory on Equip/Unequip.

src_members.sig: public UnityEvent<EquipSlotType, ItemDefinition> OnEquipmentChanged = new UnityEvent<EquipSlotType, ItemDefinition>()
src_members.name: UnityEvent
src_members.comment: slot, item now equipped there (null if that slot was just cleared).

src_members.sig: public ItemDefinition GetEquipped(EquipSlotType slot) => equipped.TryGetValue(slot, out ItemDefinition item) ? item : null
src_members.name: GetEquipped
Equip
src_members.comment: Returns false if the item isn't equippable, isn't in the inventory, or the inventory reference is missing — always check the return value rather than assuming the equip went through.

src_members.sig: public void Unequip(EquipSlotType slot) => UnequipInternal(slot, returnToInventory: true)
src_members.name: Unequip

src_members.sig: public void LoadSaveData(List<SaveEntry> data, ItemRegistry registry)
src_members.name: LoadSaveData
src_members.comment: `registry` resolves each saved itemId back to its ItemDefinition asset. Loaded items are placed directly into their slot WITHOUT touching the inventory (unlike Equip()) — the inventory's own LoadSaveData() is expected to run separately and is the authority on what's actually owned.
